text:
During the decade between 2005-2015, everyone wanted 1080p 60fps. 60fps was smooth and 1080p was good. Now our lowest end cards can dominate these settings and more.

The goalposts changed, now 1440p and higher refresh rates are becoming that same standard. I am sure over time it'll become 4k 144hz, I admit every just here is significant and pleasing.

I've never seen 8k or 300hz but from people who have they say 300hz is difficult to tell vs 144hz, and 8k is great but still can be difficult to tell from 4k. So I think 4k 144hz is probably a nice level for people to settle on before diminishing returns really set in.

So what happens to the GPU market when the 60 series card can demolish 4k 144hz? the way it currently does with 1080p 60hz? Sure it might take us another 3 or 4 generations to hit that point, but what then for the top end cards?

People buying the top end will be doing it for 8k, which you dont need, or 200+fps in demanding games, which you dont need or... some new feature they introduce?

I think NVIDIA know this, there is a diminishing point we are coming to, its why they push raytracing as a new feature to chase, because basic rasterization will sooner than later will not be enough for them to sell their top end cards.

who would need a 7090 that runs 8k, ultra, raytraced 144hz, and costs 3k when you can spend maybe $600 on a 60 series to run everything at 4k, high, medium ray traced, 120hz? maybe I am off with my numbers but the point stands, we will get to a point where the lowest end GPU does everything even the top 5% of gamers want and the true top card only cater to the 0.1%.

Right now I think pretty much everyone with a gaming PC would love a free upgrade to the current best thing because it enables a lot of siginficant graphical features. in a few more generations, if nothing major changes, I don't think that would be true anymore.
